Book correction: The book asks to show \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{-b^2x}{a^2y}. For x = a\sec t, y = b\tan t the correct result is \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{b^2x}{a^2y} (plus sign), as both methods above show. The minus sign belongs to the ellipse x = a\cos t, y = b\sin t, where \frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{b\cos t}{a\sin t} = -\frac{b^2x}{a^2y}.
